questions.question: On a floor plan, a gap in the wall with a quarter-circle shows:
options: A door and the direction it swings

questions.question: At a scale of 1 : 100, a room measuring 35 mm by 30 mm on the plan is really:
A door gap measuring 9 mm on the 1 : 100 plan is:
Measuring a room inside-face to inside-face rather than outside to outside gives:
options: The usable room size — the difference between the two is the wall thickness

subtopics.title: Elevations: the House from the Side

questions.question: The north elevation of a house is:
options: The face that looks toward the north — what a person standing to the north sees
The face that looks toward the south
Whichever face has the front door

questions.question: Elevations carry information the floor plan cannot, namely:
options: Heights — walls, roof pitch, window sills, chimneys

questions.question: The first check when matching an elevation to a side of the plan is:
options: Counting the openings — a face with two windows and a door cannot match an elevation with one window

questions.question: Viewing the north face from outside, a feature on the plan's west end appears:
options: On your right — you are facing south, so the view mirrors

subtopics.title: From Plan to Quantities and Cost

questions.question: Flooring for the 10,5 m² room with 10% waste, in boxes covering 2,2 m², needs:
Skirting for the room subtracts the doorway because:
options: Doorways are measured separately at half price
No skirting runs across an opening — 13 m of perimeter becomes 12,1 m
The door frame is wider than the wall

questions.question: The paintable wall area of 30,2 m², needing two coats at 8 m² per litre, requires:
The three-step chain for pricing anything off a plan is:
options: Measure the elevation, then the footprint, then the roof
Plan to real via the scale, real to quantity via area or perimeter, quantity to rands via pack size

subtopics.title: Models and Packaging: Cans into Boxes

questions.question: Cans of diameter 7 cm in a carton 42 cm long and 28 cm wide give one layer of:
With cans 11 cm tall in a carton 22 cm deep, the carton holds in total:
If a dimension's division gives 2,18 cans, the packing count uses:
options: 2 — round DOWN, since 0,18 of a can is only air

questions.question: Volume and surface area divide the packaging jobs as:
options: Volume for the label, surface area for the contents
Surface area for what fits, volume for what wraps
Volume for what fits inside, surface area for the cardboard that wraps it

questions.question: The door's quarter-circle matters when furnishing because:
options: It shows where the door sweeps, where a bed therefore cannot stand
It is drawn at a different scale

questions.question: The friendly arithmetic of a 1 : 100 scale is:
options: Measure in millimetres, add two zeros, and you have real millimetres

questions.question: When reporting a measurement off a plan you should always say:
options: Which lines you measured between — inside faces or outside faces

questions.question: The detective method for matching elevations starts by:
options: Listing everything touching the chosen wall on the floor plan, then finding the elevation with those openings in that order

questions.question: The mirror effect happens because:
options: Looking at the north face you are facing south, so the plan's west side is on your right
The scale reverses left and right
North is at the bottom of most plans

questions.question: The fastest clue for naming an elevation is:
options: Tall landmarks — chimney, double-storey block, lean-to — on the correct end

subtopics.title: Buying the Room, Packing the Van

questions.question: The bedroom's full materials bill — flooring R2 274, skirting R445, paint R930 — comes to:
Packing rounds DOWN per direction while shopping rounds UP because:
options: A fraction of a can is only air, but a fraction of a box short leaves the job unfinished
Packing uses volume and shopping uses area
The van is smaller than the shop

questions.question: The air in the packed carton — 25 872 cm³ minus about 20 310 cm³ of cans — is roughly:
options: A fifth of the box — the space circles always waste in rectangles

questions.question: When a packaging question turns from contents to cardboard, the correct switch is:
options: From volume, which measures what fits, to surface area, which measures what wraps
